title: When Should a Failing Robot Ask? Initiating Corrective Human-Robot Dialogue from Audited Sensor Evidence
abstract: arXiv:2609.21942v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A robot that fails at a task faces the first decision in corrective dialogue: act on its own diagnosis, consult another onboard sensor, or interrupt a person. Choosing well requires knowing how much the robot's sensors reveal about the cause and how reliable the robot's own diagnosis is. We build a simulated benchmark in which every failure's true cause is known, because we injected it, and measure what each sensor reveals, with explicit checks against data leakage. Some failures are diagnosable from camera images; others only from the robot's force data (0.99 from force data, no image method above 0.55). We then test six open vision-language models. Their behavior tracks the surface of the prompt, not the evidence: moving the refusal option from last to first in the answer list collapses refusal rates from 78-100% to 0-6% in three of the six swept model-and-family pairs. Accuracy from frames stays at or below a majority-class baseline

translated_title: 失败的机器人何时该提问？基于经审计的传感器证据启动人机纠错对话
translated_abstract: 一个在任务中失败的机器人面临纠错对话中的第一个决策：依据自身诊断采取行动、查询另一个车载传感器，还是打断人来求助。做出好的选择需要知道机器人的传感器能在多大程度上揭示故障原因，以及机器人自身诊断的可靠程度。我们构建了一个仿真基准，其中每个故障的真实原因都是已知的（因为是我们注入的），并测量每个传感器能揭示什么信息，同时进行了明确的数据泄露检查。有些故障可以通过相机图像诊断出来；另一些则只能通过机器人的力数据诊断（力数据的准确率为0.99，而没有任何图像方法超过0.55）。随后我们测试了六个开源视觉-语言模型。它们的行为跟随的是提示词的表面形式，而非证据本身：在六个被扫描的模型-模型族组合中，有三个组合在将拒绝选项从答案列表末尾移到开头后，拒绝率从78-100%骤降至0-6%。基于图像帧的准确率始终处于或低于多数类基线。
tldr: 该论文构建了一个故障原因已知的仿真基准，量化了不同传感器对机器人故障的可诊断性（力数据可达0.99而图像方法不超过0.55），并发现开源视觉-语言模型在决定是否求助时跟随提示词表面形式而非传感器证据，仅改变选项顺序就会使其拒绝率从78-100%骤降至0-6%。
en_tdlr: The paper builds a simulated benchmark with known injected failure causes to quantify sensor diagnosability (force data reaches 0.99 while no image method exceeds 0.55), and shows that open vision-language models decide whether to ask for help based on prompt surface form rather than sensor evidence, with refusal rates collapsing from 78-100% to 0-6% merely by reordering answer options.
